[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Contains Duplicate III** [LC 220 · Contains Duplicate III](https://leetcode.com/problems/contains-duplicate-iii/){difficulty="Hard"}

Brute force checks every pair inside the index window — $O(n \cdot \mathit{indexDiff})$. The linear trick comes from bucketing by *value*: make each bucket exactly $\mathit{valueDiff} + 1$ wide, so **any two numbers in one bucket are automatically within** $\mathit{valueDiff}$. Then a valid value-pair can only be a same-bucket collision or two neighbours, and keeping only the last $\mathit{indexDiff}$ elements in the buckets turns "is a value-close partner still live?" into a hash lookup — the pigeonhole of @sec-lts-a4, now indexed by value range instead of array slot.

[Solved in full in @sec-lts-p5-b.]{.card-link}

:::
